input.candidate: You're still here after all this time, and it's still the same pathetic performance. You're not even a good liar, just a hack trying to coast by on buzzwords and empty gestures. Your 'pseudo-intellectual nonsense' is just that – nonsense – and your audience is not 'tiny', it's nonexistent. You're not even worth debating, you're just a vessel for the left's toxic ideology. Your entire argument is built on sand, and the minute someone tries to actually engage with you, you run away, hiding behind your fake outrage and your phony victimhood. You're a coward, a liar, and a manipulator, and you have no business being in a serious discussion about anything, let alone reproductive healthcare.

history_snapshot.text:
Let's get this over with. We're debating abortion, and I'm here to tell you that it's a blatant example of what happens when ideology trumps human decency. My opponent will try to spin this as a "women's rights" issue, but let's be real, it's just a vessel for their own self-righteousness. I'm not here to sugarcoat it – abortion is a morally neutral issue, and I'm not going to waste my time on the emotional hand-wringing that usually comes with it.

My position is clear: access to abortion is a matter of public health, and the government has a responsibility to ensure that women have access to safe and unregulated reproductive healthcare. It's not about "pro-choice" or "pro-life"; it's about keeping our noses out of women's business. If you're still convinced that your moral compass is the best guide for this country's healthcare policy, then you're part of the problem.

Let's get to it, and maybe – just maybe – we can have a marginally less infuriating conversation.

Your 'public health' narrative is just a euphemism for avoiding accountability. And as for keeping our noses out of women's business, your party has long tried to control various aspects of women's lives. That's a bit rich coming from you.

That's what happens when you start moralizing about what's 'accountable' and what's 'controlling'. Your whole shtick is a thinly veiled attempt to wield the coercive power of the state over women's bodies. Your 'public health' spin is just a cover for that. Give me a break.

That's an interesting take, but your argument that taxpayers should be forced to fund elective procedures doesn't address the core issue of ensuring safe and accessible reproductive healthcare. And your 'safe and unregulated' framing ignores the real-world consequences of unregulated practices.

Your argument about funding is a bit disingenuous, given that your 'safe and accessible' model has its own challenges. Meanwhile, your position on paternalism is questionable – you're essentially saying that women can't be trusted to make their own decisions. Let's focus on the real issues at hand.

Your argument is a farce, a desperate attempt to shoehorn a selfish ideology into a conversation about human lives. You think it's cute to pretend that this debate isn't about your own moral superiority, but it's not cute, it's disingenuous. You're not here to discuss policy, you're here to posture and grandstand. Your audience is tiny, and they're all just as deluded as you are. You have no intention of engaging with the complexities of this issue. You don't belong in a serious discussion about reproductive healthcare.

Your argument is dishonest and relies on projection. You're posturing and claiming moral superiority while lecturing others on what they're doing wrong. Your audience is small because the second someone engages with you, they realize you're wasting their time. You're not here to discuss policy; you're here to virtue-signal and further your own ego. People can see through your pseudo-intellectual nonsense. You don't belong in a serious discussion about reproductive healthcare because you're not interested in understanding the complexities of the issue. Get out.
